## Launch the designer

```{r launch}
library(hexmakR)
hexmakr_app()
```

The default **Designer** opens a new logo with a frame and the name
"New project". It contains no archived motif. The **CTTIR Gallery** tab is an
optional source of inspiration and reusable parts.
The application title is the text **hexmakR**.

## Create your own logo

1. Enter your package or project name.
2. Choose **Hexagon**, **Pentagon** or **Square**, then a light, dark or
   monochrome appearance.
3. Keep **Blank canvas** as the base artwork, or select a generic icon.
4. Use **Apply logo settings** to update the preview.
5. Choose a circle, rectangle, line or triangle and select **Add part**.

The name stays inside the frame. **Artwork only** omits the name, while
**No frame** gives a transparent square canvas. You can add parts to that
empty canvas as well.

## Edit individual parts

Click a visible part in the preview or choose a **Selected part**. Drag and
release to move the selected artwork; use the list for overlapping or hidden
items. The list includes the frame, name, native artwork
and every added part. Highlighting helps locate the selection and is only a
preview aid; it is not included in exported artwork.

| Control | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Fill and Outline | Set a colour name or hex value; blank restores the underlying colour when the edit is applied |
| Horizontal/Vertical offset | Move the part relative to its original geometry |
| Part size | Scale the part |
| Rotation (degrees) | Rotate the part around its centre |
| Outline width and Opacity | Adjust stroke width and transparency |
| Visible | Hide or show the part |
| Edit points | Replace X/Y coordinates for the same number of points |
| Restore part | Remove the selected part's overrides |
| Duplicate part | Copy its current appearance into a new independent part |
| Remove part | Delete an added part or hide a native frame/name/artwork layer |

Choose **Apply part edit** to save changes to the selected part. Point
coordinates are local to that part's viewport. **Load original points**
loads its underlying geometry for editing. Invalid colours, nonfinite values
or mismatched point counts produce an error while retaining the last valid
logo.

Palette changes affect native design roles. Imported archive parts retain
their source colours; edit their individual fill and outline when needed.
Changing the frame, composition or base artwork retains your added parts.
Native geometry overrides are reset when their underlying structure changes.

## Name and group items

Every item has a short label. Enter a **Short name** and choose **Rename part**
to identify its purpose. The initial Frame, Icon and Name groups separate the
composition. Under **Image groups**, choose members and **Create group** or
**Set members**; **Rename group** and **Ungroup selected members** update the
organisation without changing appearance. One item belongs to one group.

Set **Mouse target** to **Whole group** to drag all members together, or use
the group movement controls. **Individual part** moves only the selected item.
The part property controls always edit the selected member. Undo and project
saves retain labels, groups and movement.

## Add a figure or vector drawing

Use **Add an image or vector drawing** to upload PNG, JPEG or SVG. Existing
work is retained and the import can be undone. PNG/JPEG is one image part:
move, scale, rotate, hide or change its opacity. Source transparency is kept.
SVG shapes and paths become separate vector parts with editable colours,
strokes and coordinates. Curves are approximated by bounded vector polylines;
SVG and PDF exports keep those vectors. Raster images stay raster in exports.

Each upload may be at most 10 MiB. Raster dimensions are capped at 8192 pixels
per side and 16 million pixels per image, with 32 million embedded pixels per
project. SVG supports solid fills/strokes, common
shapes and paths, transforms and local references. Text must be outlined;
gradients, masks, filters, group opacity and intersecting clips must first be
flattened to paths. Unsupported features return an explanation. Scripts,
external resources and XML entities are rejected. Imported files are embedded
as image bytes or vector coordinates, so reopening a project does not need
the original upload.

## Reuse archive artwork

Open **CTTIR Gallery** and select an identity. The preview and part list update;
your current logo and undo history stay unchanged.

- **Add selected part to my logo** imports just the chosen native component.
- **Add artwork to my logo** imports the motif's components, excluding its
  frame and package name.
- **Start from whole design** replaces the current logo with that archived
  composition. This is a separate explicit action; **Undo** restores your work.

Imports retain your current name, frame, palette and existing parts. Imported
components remain individually editable and use a saved source snapshot.
They do not change when you later browse a different archive identity.

```{r preselect-archive}
hexmakr_app(package = "phenoscapR")
```

The `package` argument preselects an archive identity. The Designer still
starts with a fresh logo.

## Undo, reset and reopen

**Undo** restores the previous applied action, including New logo, archive
replacement and opening a project. The editor retains up to 30 undo steps.
**Reset to starting design** returns to the current baseline: the fresh
project, the explicitly loaded archive design, or the opened JSON project.
**New logo** starts another blank composition.

**Save project** downloads editable JSON. **Open saved project** restores its
settings, primitives, uploaded artwork, imported archive parts, labels, groups
and individual edits. Only the
supported data schema is accepted; project loading does not execute R code.
Saved and loaded projects share a 20 MiB size limit.

## Export

PNG, SVG and PDF use the currently applied design. Choose the PNG width in
pixels; vector exports retain outlined paths and names. **R recipe** writes
code that reproduces the same project. Pending settings must be applied
before downloading.

For a package README or pkgdown site, place the named SVG/PNG at
`man/figures/logo.svg` and `man/figures/logo.png`. Use the matching named dark
variant at `man/figures/logo-dark.svg`. Keep the package name inside the image.

## Classic designer

```{r classic}
hexmakr_app(workspace = "classic")
```

The classic workspace retains its live ggplot preview, 46 icons, PNG/JPEG
upload, subtitle/URL controls and PNG export. Its 28 theme presets list the
nine CTTIR v5 families first, under **CTTIR v5**, followed by the 19 generic
themes. Its 14 font choices include the bundled JetBrains Mono used for v5
names. Use it for existing generic-sticker workflows; the default Designer
provides individually editable vector parts and portable projects.
